boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Ithaca College spaces for studying, gathering, recreation, art, reflection, and time outdoors, each supported by a direct college source.

cards.title: Match the Floor to the Work
cards.subtitle: Quiet zones, group rooms, and social space in Gannett Center
cards.notes: Choose a quiet seat for solo work, reserve a room for group projects, or use the designated areas for lunch, games, and conversation.
cards.short_summary: A multi-mode study hub with 602 seats and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The library reports 602 seats and spaces for quiet study, reservable group work, games, lunch, and meeting friends.
cards.access_notes: Library access and individual space rules apply; consult the library website for current hours and room reservations.

cards.title: Bring a Laptop—or Just Lunch
cards.subtitle: A third-floor Campus Center lounge built for flexible downtime
cards.notes: Use the three computers, settle in with lunch, study between commitments, or connect a video to the projector while the building is open.
cards.short_summary: A casual student lounge combining computers, seating, and a projector.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca College identifies the third-floor Unity Student Lounge as a place to study, eat lunch, meet students, use three computers, or watch videos on its projector.
cards.access_notes: The lounge is open while the Campus Center is open; follow Unity Center and Campus Center policies.

cards.title: Reset in Room 202
cards.subtitle: A student self-care room inside the Fitness Center
cards.notes: Stop in to use a meditation pillow, light-therapy box, yoga mat, coloring materials, or another sensory resource during Fitness Center hours.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated pause point stocked with practical relaxation tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The college’s Spring 2026 resource guide describes Fitness Center Room 202 as a student wellness space with light-therapy boxes, meditation pillows, puzzles, and other self-care supplies.
cards.source_title: Student Affairs & Campus Life Resource Guide
cards.access_notes: Located in Fitness Center Room 202 and available during Fitness Center hours; campus access rules may require an Ithaca College ID.

cards.title: Make the Break Interactive
cards.subtitle: Games and informal hangout space downstairs in the Campus Center
cards.notes: Head downstairs for Ping-Pong, foosball, air hockey, pool tables, or a shared-screen break when you have time between campus commitments.
cards.short_summary: An indoor game room for active, low-key breaks with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Campus Center place page says its downstairs recreation center includes a big-screen television, air hockey, Ping-Pong, foosball, and pool tables.
cards.access_notes: Use during Campus Center operating hours and follow posted recreation-equipment and building rules.

cards.title: Claim a Between-Class Landing Spot
cards.subtitle: One of the Campus Center’s named student lounges
cards.notes: Use this named lounge for a short study session or conversation between classes, checking the room first for any scheduled campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A central lounge suited to brief study sessions and meetups.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca College lists Clark Lounge among the Campus Center’s event spaces and describes it as a place to relax between classes.
cards.access_notes: Availability can change for scheduled events; use the lounge only while the Campus Center is open and the room is available.

cards.title: Meet in a Room Everyone Can Name
cards.subtitle: A reservable Campus Center lounge and everyday gathering point
cards.notes: Name Klingenstein as the meetup point, then use the lounge to talk or work if it is not reserved for a campus meeting or event.
cards.short_summary: A clearly named gathering room that simplifies group coordination.
cards.evidence_claim: The college identifies Klingenstein Lounge as a Campus Center event space and names it among the lounges used to relax between classes.
cards.access_notes: The room may be reserved for events or meetings; check availability and observe current Campus Center hours and policies.

cards.title: Use the Ball as Your Pin Drop
cards.subtitle: The 1967 sculpture that doubles as a campus meeting point
cards.notes: Set the sculpture as an outdoor meetup landmark, then pause for the campus view before heading together to class or another destination.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive sculpture with a documented second life as a social landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca College’s anniversary archive says the 1967 Textor Disc, commonly called the Textor Ball, remains a central place where students spend time with friends before and after class.
cards.access_notes: The sculpture is outdoors near Textor Hall; remain in public campus areas and do not climb on or alter the artwork.

cards.title: Put Art at the Center of the Conversation
cards.subtitle: A Gannett Center gallery designed as a gathering space
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition before visiting, then use the displayed work as the starting point for a conversation or creative break.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery where rotating exhibitions create a shared focal point.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca College calls Handwerker Gallery a space to gather with art at the center and documents students discussing work in its exhibitions.
cards.access_notes: Check the exhibition page before visiting; the gallery closes between installations and its hours can change for special weekends.

cards.title: Find a Quieter Kind of Gathering
cards.subtitle: A pond-facing sanctuary used for reflection and campus programs
cards.notes: Join a scheduled meditation session or use an appropriate public program to experience the wood-lined gathering space overlooking the pond.
cards.short_summary: A nonsectarian campus space shared through meditation, services, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The college describes Muller Chapel as a nonsectarian, pond-facing sanctuary used for organized meditation, religious services, concerts, and other events.
cards.access_notes: Attend during a posted public program or confirmed open period; respect services, private events, and the quiet purpose of the space.

cards.title: Trade the Quad for a Woodland Loop
cards.subtitle: A student-improved route in the Ithaca College Natural Lands
cards.notes: Start near Boothroyd Hall, review conditions at the trailhead, and take the improved approach into the Natural Lands with a companion.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge woodland route shaped through student stewardship.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca College documents a student-led accessibility project at Boothroyd Woods Trail, including an improved approach near Boothroyd Hall and its use by campus and community members.
cards.source_title: Improving Access to the IC Natural Lands | Ithaca College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and trail surfaces vary; use marked routes in daylight, check weather, and note that accessibility is limited beyond improved sections.
